title: Cross-SDK graceful socket shutdown and connection reuse patterns cookbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: SDK users frequently encounter subtle failures when servers close sockets or when the client reuses connections while a prior streaming response is still draining. This leads to broken streaming ergonomics, spurious retries, head-of-line stalls, and elevated P95 latency in real workloads. Goal: Produce a cross-SDK cookbook (Python/TypeScript/Go) describing pragmatic, tested patterns for graceful socket shutdown, proactive connection health-checks, keepalive tuning, and safe connection reuse that reduce spurious errors and improve streaming reliability across hosted and dedicated deployments. Deliverables: - A single developer-oriented doc with per-language examples (idiomatic code snippets) and recommended default config values. - Runtime telemetry knobs to detect stale connections, half-closed sockets, and server-initiated resets. - Test harness (unit + integration checklist) and example PRs implementing the patterns in each SDK.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical cookbook page committed in SDK repo docs with language sections for Python, TypeScript, and Go
Per-language example PRs created and merged with no behavioral regressions in CI
Benchmarks showing reduced streaming error rate (>= 50% reduction in flaky stream disconnects) on synthetic workload
Telemetry events emitted for socket-reset, graceful-shutdown, keepalive-probe-failures, and reused-stale-connection with documentation for alerting rules
E2E checklist for integrators and customers included in the doc (how to tune for long polls vs short requests)
implementation_notes: Python: use urllib3/httpx pool manager hooks to detect EOF on read and mark connection as 'do-not-reuse' instead of immediate reconnect; recommend default keepalive interval 30s and idle timeout 90s in hosted environments; show example using httpx.AsyncClient with transport parameters and a small retry wrapper that distinguishes Idempotent vs Streaming calls

TypeScript: for Node fetch/got clients, demonstrate agent.keepAlive = true with socketTimeout and freeSocketKeepAliveTimeout adjustments; implement a per-request 'streamingLease' that pins a connection while stream active and signals graceful shutdown via 'socket.end' semantics; provide example wrapper around fetch that returns an AbortController and cleans up on server reset

Go: recommend net/http Transport with MaxIdleConnsPerHost tuned to concurrency shape, IdleConnTimeout default 60s, and custom DialContext wrapper that sets TCP keepalive to 30s; provide pattern for Request.WithContext cancellation to trigger half-close and safe reuse detection by draining response.Body with io.Copy to io.Discard when we intend to reuse; show how to detect 'connection: close' header and proactively mark transport to not reuse connection

Retry behavior: do not apply automatic retries for streaming responses; for non-streaming idempotent requests, prefer fast failover and backoff; document how to synthesize deadlines so retries do not extend overall user-visible timeout (use per-attempt budgets).

Backpressure and draining: include pattern to buffer a small prefix (e.g., first 8KB) of streaming responses to detect early errors while preserving low latency for streaming consumers; when upstream signals shutdown, ensure client drains before reusing socket or explicitly close to avoid corrupted pipelined responses

Socket shutdown primitives: discuss SO_LINGER, shutdown(SHUT_WR), and how each SDK's runtime maps to those primitives; recommend avoiding SO_LINGER for normal flows and prefer orderly half-close where supported

Testing: include a small harness that kills server socket mid-stream, sends FIN-only, and simulates delayed FIN to validate client reuse heuristics. Add unit tests that assert connection marked unusable after certain read errors.
progress_updates: 2025-02-21: Initial discovery notes and field reports collected from SDK support channels; reproduced flaky stream reset locally using standalone toy server (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/219)
2025-02-25: Draft cookbook outline committed to repo at docs/transport/cookbook-graceful-shutdown.md (WIP) - see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/223
2025-02-28: Python and Go example implementations prototyped; TypeScript agent behavior needs additional testing on Node 18 vs Node 20 (TLS socket semantics differ)
2025-03-03: Telemetry schema proposed (events: socket_reset, keepalive_probe_failed, half_close_detected, stale_reuse_blocked) - awaiting instrumentation review

2025-03-05: Integration tests added to SDK CI (flaky-stream-kill scenario). Observed 60% reduction in stream disconnects in synthetic runner when client drains vs immediate reuse. Preparing PRs per SDK for code changes.
review_feedback: PM (Lina Cho) asked to include guidance for Dedicated vs Hosted defaults — added note section mapping defaults to deployment profiles
Security review: insist on not lowering TLS socket timeouts; instrumentation must not log raw tokens or payloads — added masking guidance
Design: request clearer UX text for streaming aborts so library consumers can distinguish user-initiated vs network-initiated closures
Runtime team: suggested adding an optional 'connection_safety_probe' telemetry event emitted from runtime when a reused connection was previously half-closed
risks_mitigation: Risk: aggressive keepalive/idle settings may increase NAT table churn for mobile customers. Mitigation: provide conservative mobile presets and emphasize tuning guides for different network topologies.
Risk: adding client-side draining adds CPU/io overhead. Mitigation: make draining an opt-in pattern for high-throughput non-purely-idempotent flows and provide benchmarks.
Risk: behavioral diffs across Node/Python/Go may confuse users. Mitigation: keep cookbook explicit per-language and add cross-reference table of semantic differences.
notes_for_oncall: If an incident references repeated 'Broken pipe' or 'connection reset by peer' during streaming, consult this cookbook and check for the 'stale_reuse_blocked' events in transport telemetry
Oncall should consider toggling 'force_connection_close_on_stream_termination' in runtime feature flags if a customer experiences immediate reuse corruption while SDK updates roll out
